Read a stream

Ollama Streaming API

Set "stream":true and read the response in the format used by your endpoint. Ollama’s /api/chat sends one JSON object per line. Its OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions sends Server-Sent Events. Check the terminal marker and the finish reason before saving the reply as complete.

  1. Read native JSON lines
  2. Read OpenAI-compatible SSE
  3. Detect a cut-off or token-limited response
  4. Compare the actual captured streams

Which stream does your client use?

See stepsSee stepsSee steps

Stream native /api/chat with curl

Download request-native.json and set model to an installed tag. Send the file to your local server. The example uses a text-only prompt, one response and no tools.

curl --noproxy '*' -fsSN \
  http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/chat \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary @request-native.json > native.ndjson

Ollama sends application/x-ndjson. Parse each complete line as JSON and append message.content exactly as received. A network chunk may contain part of a line or several lines. The done frame can carry an empty text fragment and still contain done_reason and counts. For /api/generate, use response for the text instead.

Read SSE from /v1/chat/completions

Download request-compatible.json and set the same local tag. This route returns text/event-stream. The request also asks for usage with stream_options.include_usage.

curl --noproxy '*' -fsSN \
  http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary @request-compatible.json > compatible.sse

Process complete SSE events separated by blank lines. For a JSON payload, append choices[0].delta.content when it exists. The finish reason is on the choice. A usage event can arrive with an empty choices array after the finish reason. Continue until the data: [DONE] event, which is a marker outside JSON. Use the local OpenAI SDK guide if an SDK is handling SSE for you.

Know when the text is ready to use

  1. For native chat, look for done: true and read done_reason. For compatible chat, require both the choice’s finish reason and the [DONE] event in the tested Ollama stream.
  2. Check whether the finish reason is suitable for your application. Both test streams reached their terminal markers with reason length at a one-token limit. Each contained only LOCAL from the intended reply LOCAL_OK.
  3. If the connection closes before the terminal marker, treat the text as incomplete. If the stream contains an error record, handle it before using any text. In a streaming UI, add incoming text as a preview and mark it complete only after the final checks.

curl -N disables curl’s own output buffering. To watch the raw events as they arrive, omit the file redirection. If events still arrive together, check your client’s read method and try the same request directly on loopback to isolate buffering outside the application.

For a saved response, download read-chat-stream.py and run it with Python 3.9 or later. This example prints buffered text only after a normal stop. It handles one text chat choice. Tool calls and reasoning events require separate handling.

python3 read-chat-stream.py native native.ndjson
python3 read-chat-stream.py compatible compatible.sse

When you only need one short structured result, use a non-streaming JSON Schema request and validate the result.
